name: OpSystem
summary: A field command and evidence system for police response units, rapid response vehicles and mobile command posts. Officers open incidents, watch social, video, broadcast and cellular panels, seal evidence with SHA-256, and run search, OSINT collection and AI reports against OpSystem Core.
gettingAccess: A commanding officer (super user) invites you from the Team panel in the Analysis desk. You receive a one-use enrolment link, valid for 24 hours, and paste it on the ENROLMENT LINK tab of the sign-in screen, or sign in with the account a commander issued you. In this build the app runs in the desktop (Electron) and Android apps; opened in an ordinary browser it shows only the OpSystem logo. Never share enrolment links, device tokens or gate keys outside a channel your unit trusts.

guides.title: Sign in or enrol this device
guides.goal: Get this desktop or phone onto OpSystem with your own operator account.
before: You have an issued account, or an enrolment link from a commander.
You are using the desktop or Android app.
steps: Open OpSystem. On a device with no saved session the app opens as its built-in default super-user profile, not the sign-in screen. Click SIGN OUT in the header to reach the sign-in screen (OPSYSTEM · C4ISR TERMINAL) and sign in as yourself before doing any work.
To enrol with a link: click ENROLMENT LINK, paste the link into ENROLMENT LINK PAYLOAD, and click ENROL & ENTER TACTICAL GRID.

To sign in with an issued account: stay on OPERATOR SIGN IN, enter your OFFICER / LO NUMBER or POLICE EMAIL / IDENTITY and your OPERATIONAL SECURITY PIN / PASSWORD, complete the station and rank fields, and click AUTHENTICATE & ENTER C4ISR COMMAND CENTER.
Check the header: your name and the VEHICLE STATION badge show who is signed in on this device.
To leave, click SIGN OUT in the header.
guides.result: The tactical grid opens and the device keeps its own token, so it reconnects by itself next time.

troubleshooting.problem: Invalid OpSystem enrolment link. Please verify the QR/link payload.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the whole link exactly as you received it. Links are single-use and expire after 24 hours; ask the commander for a new one.

troubleshooting.problem: Opened in a browser, only the logo appears
troubleshooting.fix: The browser build is closed in this version. Use the desktop or Android app.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in with your LO number fails
troubleshooting.fix: The core looks operators up by email. Enter your POLICE EMAIL / IDENTITY instead of the LO number.

guides.title: Choose a layout and focus a panel
guides.goal: Arrange the screen for the job: four panels, three, two, or one full-screen panel.
steps: In the header, click a layout button: QUAD (alerts, video, social and news), 3-SPLIT, DUAL, VIDEO GRID, SOCIAL INTEL, MAP / HOTSPOTS, MISSING PERSONS, ANALYSIS or ADMIN. On narrower screens pick the same choices from the layout dropdown (QUAD 4-SPLIT, 3-SPLIT DOMINANT, DUAL SPLIT and so on).
In DUAL, use SELECT: to choose the panel on each side, and ⇄ SWAP to swap them.
To enlarge one panel, use its focus button (for example Focus Video Panel or Focus GSM Telemetry). The panel fills the screen under FULL VIEW FOCUS.
Click RESTORE MULTI-VIEW to go back to the grid. Full-page views such as SOCIAL INTEL, MISSING PERSONS and ADMINISTRATION have BACK TO GRID or RETURN TO GRID instead.
On a phone (below 768 px wide) one panel shows at a time; switch with the bottom tabs ALERTS, PERSONS, SOCIAL, VIDEO, NEWS, GSM and ANALYSE.
Use Toggle fullscreen in the header for a vehicle display.
guides.result: The grid shows the panels you chose, and the choice stays until you change it.

troubleshooting.problem: A panel shows Tactical Grid Fault
troubleshooting.fix: That panel failed to draw; the reset returns you to the QUAD layout. Try the layout again.

guides.title: Launch a new incident
guides.goal: Open an incident with a callsign, priority, geofence and watch keywords, so evidence and monitoring attach to it.
before: The app shows CORE online (an incident is created on OpSystem Core).
steps: With no active incident, click 1-CLICK SITUATION DISPATCH / DRIVE OUT in the incident bar; with one already active, click NEW SITUATION.

Optionally pick a preset from ⚡ SELECT HIGH-RISK SITUATION PRESET TO LOAD... to fill the form, or describe the situation in the AI SITUATION ASSIST box and click AI AUTO-FILL. AI AUTO-FILL sends the brief from this device to an external AI service, and any field the model leaves out is filled with a fixed default (threat priority CRITICAL, a default Gauteng location and coordinates, a 15 km radius), so check every field before launching.
Enter the TACTICAL INCIDENT TITLE and COMMAND CALLSIGN, and choose the THREAT PRIORITY (CRITICAL, HIGH or MEDIUM).

Enter the OPERATIONAL LOCATION NAME. Use the INTERACTIVE OPENSTREETMAP GEOFENCE PICKER (search and click FIND, or click/drag on the map) to set LATITUDE (WGS-84) and LONGITUDE (WGS-84), then set the GEOFENCE RADIUS.
Enter the 24/7 MONITORED SITUATIONAL KEYWORDS (COMMA-SEPARATED) and a TACTICAL INCIDENT SUMMARY.
Click LAUNCH INVESTIGATION & DRIVE OUT.
guides.result: The incident bar shows the new incident with its title, ID, callsign, geofence and first keywords, and its status is ACTIVE_DISPATCH.

troubleshooting.problem: The launch fails
troubleshooting.fix: The core must be reachable and the title is required. Check the core connection in the Analysis desk (gear icon).

troubleshooting.problem: The form came back as CRITICAL with a location you did not give
troubleshooting.fix: Those are AI AUTO-FILL's defaults for fields the model left empty. Correct the priority, location, coordinates and radius by hand.

guides.title: Respond to a critical public safety alert
guides.goal: Turn a critical alert into an active incident in one step, or dismiss it.
before: A CRITICAL PUBLIC SAFETY ALERT banner is showing under the header.
steps: Read the alert title, summary and the VIA: line naming where it came from.
To respond, click 1-CLICK LAUNCH & DRIVE OUT. An incident is created from the alert's title, location, geofence, keywords and summary.
If it does not need a response, click Dismiss Alert.
Alerts also appear in the Active alerts panel (ALERTS on a phone), where they can be dismissed the same way.
guides.result: The alert leaves the banner and, if launched, the incident bar shows the new incident.

guides.title: Track, stand down, contain or reactivate an incident
guides.goal: Move an incident through its states without losing its evidence.
steps: Click LIVE MAP in the incident bar to show the live tracking map; click HIDE MAP to close it.

Once an incident is 48 hours old (counted from when it was opened), the app asks whether active operations should stand down (48-HOUR ACTIVE POLICING TIMEOUT // CASE STATUS, and a 48-HOUR ACTIVE WINDOW EXCEEDED line in the incident bar). Choose ✓ MARK AS INACTIVE (STILL OPEN) to stand down while the investigation continues. KEEP ACTIVE (AUTHORISE EXTENSION) / KEEP ACTIVE only hides the prompt on this device; it records no extension anywhere, so record the decision in the case notes.
To bring an inactive incident back, click REACTIVATE. This does not restart the 48-hour clock, which still runs from when the incident was opened.

When the incident is contained, click CONTAIN & LOCK to mark it contained and seal its active evidence docket. There is no confirmation step, so be sure before you click; the core still accepts evidence for the incident afterwards.
guides.result: The STATUS in the incident bar changes accordingly. The docket and its sealed exhibits stay open and preserved when an incident is marked inactive.

guides.title: Watch the social stream and seal a post as evidence
guides.goal: Follow posts for the active incident and lock a relevant post into the evidence docket.
steps: Find the social panel in the grid (SOCIAL on a phone). It shows posts the core holds for the active incident.
Read ATTENTION VELOCITY: the posts-per-minute over the last five minutes against the last hour, with status NORMAL, ELEVATED or CRITICAL_SPIKE.
Filter by platform (ALL PLATFORMS, CRIME REPORTERS (X), X / TWITTER, TELEGRAM, TIKTOK, FACEBOOK). To watch extra words, type them and press Enter, or click ADD.
On a post, click SEAL TO DOCKET. The button reads SEALING... and then SEALED IN DOCKET.
Use VERIFY AT SOURCE to open the original post, or REVERSE LOOKUP IN OSINT to send its photo to the Analysis desk.
guides.result: The post is hashed with SHA-256 on this device, stored in the local docket, and uploaded to the core with that hash; the DOCKET count in the header goes up.

troubleshooting.problem: NO SOCIAL POSTS CURRENTLY MATCHING ACTIVE CRITERIA
troubleshooting.fix: The stream shows only posts that have reached the core for this incident; nothing is invented. Add posts through SOCIAL INTEL, or widen the platform filter.

guides.title: Capture a video snapshot or clip as evidence
guides.goal: Grab a frame or a 15-second clip from a camera or stream, sealed with SHA-256.
before: Desktop or Android app with camera permission granted.
An incident is active if the evidence should go to the core.
steps: Find the TACTICAL VIDEO STREAM & OPTICAL SURVEILLANCE panel (VIDEO on a phone).
Choose the source with Select from additional tactical video feeds; click Rescan cameras after plugging in a camera.
Click GRAB SNAPSHOT to seal the current frame.
Click RECORD CLIP to record 15 seconds; the button reads RECORDING until it finishes.
Read the notice: it gives the local SHA-256 and either core verified (the core stored the same bytes) or CORE HASH MISMATCH.
guides.result: The frame or clip is saved to this device's evidence folder with a chain-of-custody line, and appears in the DOCKET.

troubleshooting.problem: NO TACTICAL VIDEO SOURCE or "no camera attached"
troubleshooting.fix: Attach a camera and click Rescan cameras. On macOS, re-enable Camera access for OpSystem in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Camera if it was denied.

troubleshooting.problem: TACTICAL FEED OFFLINE // DEVICE NOT CONNECTED
troubleshooting.fix: The selected feed has no live source. Choose another feed.

guides.title: Review and export the evidence docket
guides.goal: Check every sealed item for the incident and export the docket.
steps: Click DOCKET in the header (the number beside it is the item count).
The POLICE INCIDENT EVIDENCE DOCKET opens for the active incident (or GENERAL EVIDENCE VAULT if none is active).

For each item, read SHA-256, RECORDED BY and SOURCE, and use Copy SHA-256 Hash to copy a hash. The "✓ SEAL VERIFIED" label appears on every item whether or not the core confirmed the hash, so do not rely on it: only the notice shown at capture ("core verified" or "CORE HASH MISMATCH") reflects the core's check.
Click EXPORT DOSSIER to download the docket as OPSYSTEM-DOCKET-<incident id>.json.
Close the docket when done.
guides.result: A JSON file of the docket is saved, listing each item with its hash and custody details.

troubleshooting.problem: NO EVIDENCE ITEMS SEALED IN THIS DOCKET YET.
troubleshooting.fix: Capture posts, video snapshots or broadcast frames from the grid first.

troubleshooting.problem: RECORDED BY shows an officer other than you
troubleshooting.fix: Items sealed on the device record the app's built-in default profile rather than the signed-in officer; the core stamps the signed-in operator only on items it receives with the device's own token. Note the correct officer in the case record.

guides.title: Read cellular telemetry and send a field SMS
guides.goal: Check the vehicle modem's signal and cell, and send an order to a ground unit by SMS.
before: Desktop or Android app with a USB LTE modem attached.
steps: Find the GSM MODEM & CELLULAR TELEMETRY panel (GSM on a phone).
Read CARRIER & OPERATOR, SIGNAL STRENGTH (RSSI) and the CELL TOWER TELEMETRY fields CELL ID (CID), LOC AREA (LAC) and PLMN (MCC-MNC).
Watch the integrity line: CELLULAR RF INTEGRITY: NO ANOMALY SIGNATURE, or CRITICAL: RF DENIAL / ROGUE TOWER SIGNATURE.
Under TACTICAL GSM MODEM SMS DISPATCH, enter the number (+27…) and the field order (up to 160 characters), and click DISPATCH.
Read the confirmation SMS ACCEPTED BY MODEM — message reference ...
guides.result: The modem accepts the SMS, and if an incident is active a GSM log entry is added to its docket.

troubleshooting.problem: NO LTE MODEM ANSWERING AT COMMANDS
troubleshooting.fix: No modem was found on the serial ports the app tried. Check the USB connection; on Android, allow USB permission when asked.

troubleshooting.problem: The rogue tower warning appears
troubleshooting.fix: It is a heuristic from consecutive readings (for example a drop from LTE to GSM, or a cell change without an area change), not a certified detector. Report it through your unit's procedure.

guides.title: Search the core and collect an OSINT source
guides.goal: Find anything the core holds, and add a public web page to the active incident.
before: The Analysis desk shows CORE online.
steps: Click ANALYSIS in the header (ANALYSE tab on a phone), then SITREP & CORE REPORTS.
Type into search evidence, OSINT, posts, reports and click Search the core. End a word with * to match its prefix (for example grayston*).
Read each result's kind, title, score and snippet.
Under COLLECT OSINT SOURCE, paste a page address and click FETCH. The line beside the heading tells you whether it will be attached to the active incident.
Watch the job list for the outcome; click Refresh if needed.
guides.result: The fetched page is stripped to text, categorised and indexed on the core, and becomes searchable and part of the incident dossier.

troubleshooting.problem: Connect to the core to search.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the core address in the gear-icon panel (see Connect to OpSystem Core and manage your team).

troubleshooting.problem: The fetch job fails
troubleshooting.fix: The core refuses private and loopback addresses and pages it cannot read. Use a public URL.

guides.title: Run an AI report or ask the dossier
guides.goal: Produce a SITREP, action plan, timeline, entity list or OSINT leads from the incident's evidence, or ask it a question.
before: The Analysis desk header shows AI with a model name (not AI NOT CONFIGURED ON CORE).
steps: Open ANALYSIS, then SITREP & CORE REPORTS.
Look at the DOSSIER section for the active incident's counts and category chips; click DOSSIER to export the full text the AI reads.
Click a report button: SITREP, ACTION PLAN, TIMELINE, ENTITIES or OSINT LEADS.
To ask a question, type it in Ask the dossier: ... and click ASK.
Read the report in the list; reports cite evidence IDs and separate what is verified from what is reported.
guides.result: A new report appears for the incident.

troubleshooting.problem: The report buttons are disabled and the header says AI NOT CONFIGURED ON CORE
troubleshooting.fix: The core has no AI provider configured. The app never produces a report without one; ask the core's administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: Open an incident (NEW SITUATION) to build a dossier and run analysis.
troubleshooting.fix: Launch or reactivate an incident first.

guides.title: Connect to OpSystem Core and manage your team
guides.goal: Point this device at the right core, and (as a commander) invite operators, disable them and revoke devices.
guides.role: Commander (SUPER_USER) for the team steps; any operator for the connection
steps: Open ANALYSIS and click Core connection and team (the gear icon).

Enter the core address, the device token or static key, and (only where the core sits behind a UAT gate) the gate access key, then click APPLY. The header line then reads CORE followed by the address, or CORE OFFLINE.
As a super user, use TEAM — OPERATORS & DEVICES below: enter email, name, role (OFFICER, ANALYST or SUPER_USER) and LO number, and click INVITE.
Click COPY on the Enrolment link for ... box and send it over a channel you trust. It is single-use and shows when it expires; it carries this terminal's gate key.
To stop an operator, click Disable (ends every device) on their row; click again to Enable. To cut off one device, click Revoke this device.
To remove this device from the core, use Disconnect this device (revokes its token).
guides.result: The device talks to the chosen core, and the team list shows each operator with their role and active devices.

troubleshooting.problem: The team section is missing
troubleshooting.fix: It appears only for an operator with the SUPER_USER role.

troubleshooting.problem: CORE OFFLINE after APPLY
troubleshooting.fix: Check the address and key with your administrator. On a phone, the address is the vehicle terminal's, not the phone's own.

guides.title: File and work a missing person dossier
guides.goal: Register a missing person, add sightings and evidence, and run an OSINT scan.
steps: Click MISSING PERSONS in the header. The MISSING PERSONS & OSINT HUB lists cases; filter with ALL STATUSES, ACTIVE SEARCH, ★ CONCLUSIVE, LEAD FOUND, LOCATED or CLOSED, or Search name, ID....

Click FILE MISSING PERSON. Fill in FULL LEGAL NAME, identity details, physical description, LAST SEEN DATE & TIME, LAST SEEN LOCATION, DISAPPEARANCE CIRCUMSTANCES, CLOTHING WORN WHEN LAST SEEN and PRIORITY, and attach a SUBJECT PHOTOGRAPH.
Click REGISTER DOSSIER & START OSINT.
Select the case and click RUN DEEP OSINT SCAN to run the automated crawl and border checks; results appear under REAL-TIME OSINT & SIGHTING INTERCEPTS.

To add a sighting, click UPLOAD EVIDENCE, choose the EVIDENCE SOURCE and MEDIA CATEGORY, enter the EVIDENCE TITLE, DETAILED NARRATIVE & SIGHTING CONTEXT and LOCATION, attach the file and click SEAL & SUBMIT EVIDENCE.
Tick FLAG AS POTENTIALLY CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE only when the evidence may resolve the case, and give the CONCLUSIVE CORROBORATION REASON. This alerts every connected unit.
Click DOSSIER to download the case's sealed investigative dossier.
guides.result: The case appears in the hub with its evidence sealed by SHA-256; a conclusive flag raises the POTENTIALLY CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE ALERT banner on connected terminals, with FOCUS MISSING PERSON HUB to open it.

troubleshooting.problem: No active missing person cases match criteria.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the filter to ALL STATUSES and clear the search box.

guides.title: Follow crime reporters and ingest on-scene posts
guides.goal: Monitor chosen accounts and add a post from an active situation to the incident.
steps: Click SOCIAL INTEL in the header. The CRIME DESK INTEL · MONITORED SOCIAL WIRE desk opens.

To monitor an account, click FOLLOW NEW ACCOUNT, enter ACCOUNT HANDLE *, NAME / DESK, PLATFORM (X / Twitter, News Desk / RSS or Mastodon), OUTLET, CRIME BEAT and PROFILE URL, and click FOLLOW & MONITOR.
Filter accounts by Account Status (ALL STATUS, ACTIVE ONLY, PAUSED ONLY) and the INTERCEPT FEED by THREAT FILTER (ALL THREATS, CRITICAL ONLY, HIGH ONLY, CORRELATED TO INCIDENTS).

To add a post from the scene, click INGEST ACTIVE SITUATION POST, fill in ACCOUNT / DISPATCHER HANDLE *, POST TEXT / CRIME SCENE REPORT *, LOCATION NAME and ORIGINAL POST URL, choose the ATTACHMENT TYPE, tick the box to seal it into the active incident's docket if wanted, and click INGEST & TRIGGER ALARM.
Click BACK TO GRID when done.
guides.result: Followed accounts appear in the account list; an ingested post appears in the intercept feed, and posts matching the active incident are marked 🎯 CORRELATED WITH ACTIVE INCIDENT.

troubleshooting.problem: A HIGH THREAT SOCIAL INTERCEPT banner appears elsewhere in the app
troubleshooting.fix: Click FOCUS SOCIAL WIRE to open this desk on it, or dismiss it with ✕.

guides.title: Use the Gauteng hotspot map
guides.goal: See recent crime alerts by sector and launch an incident in a hotspot.
steps: Click MAP / HOTSPOTS in the header.

Choose the WINDOW (PAST 1 HOUR to ALL TIME (24H+)) and the REGION (ALL GAUTENG (PROVINCE-WIDE), JHB METRO, TSHWANE / PTA, EKURHULENI, WEST RAND or SEDIBENG), or type in Search sectors, stations, alerts, keywords....
Switch the base map with DARK, SAT or OSM, and toggle TRAFFIC and HOTSPOTS overlays.
Click a sector and use ZOOM TO SECTOR; read SAPS CLUSTER, PATROL RADIUS, ACTIVE 24H ALERTS and PRIORITY CRIMES.
Click LAUNCH TACTICAL SITUATION IN THIS HOTSPOT to open the incident launcher pre-filled for that sector, or INVESTIGATE IN OSINT to take an image to the Analysis desk.
Click GRID to return to the multi-view grid.
guides.result: The map shows alerts in the chosen window and region, and the launcher opens with the hotspot's details when you launch from it.

troubleshooting.problem: No verified crime alerts in this time window.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a longer WINDOW or a wider REGION.

guides.title: Install OpSystem on a Mac, Windows or Android device
guides.goal: Put the desktop or Android app on a vehicle terminal or phone.
before: The OpSystem project folder with dependencies installed (npm install).
For Android: the Android SDK and JDK 21.
steps: macOS: run ./start.sh install. It builds the app, removes any previous OpSystem.app, and installs the new one; open it from /Applications.
The macOS bundle is unsigned: the first time, right-click the app and choose Open. Allow Camera access when macOS asks.
To make an installer to copy to another Mac or a Linux terminal, run ./start.sh package (a .dmg and .zip on macOS; AppImage and .deb on Linux).
Windows: with Node.js 22, run npm ci, then npm run package:win; run the generated OpSystem installer, which creates a desktop shortcut.
Android: run ./start.sh android to build a debug APK (installed automatically if a device is connected over adb), or ./start.sh android release for an unsigned release APK.
Open the app and sign in or enrol (see Sign in or enrol this device).
guides.result: OpSystem opens on the device at the sign-in screen.

troubleshooting.problem: macOS says the app cannot be opened
troubleshooting.fix: It is unsigned. Right-click → Open the first time.

troubleshooting.problem: Camera reads as denied on macOS
troubleshooting.fix: Re-enable it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Camera. Launching the app from a non-interactive shell suppresses the prompt.

troubleshooting.problem: RTL-SDR or DVB panels say unsupported on a phone
troubleshooting.fix: Those devices are not supported on Android; the panels say so by design.
